title: Reduce metric cardinality for kernel_choice telemetry (selector v2)
author: Omar El-Sayed
description: Context: After enabling selector v2 in internal canary, we saw a sharp increase in Prometheus/Mimir series and query latency on the runtime perf dashboards. Root cause is high-cardinality label sets on the kernel selection metrics (notably per-kernel id and per-model id variants). This PR makes kernel selection telemetry conform to the cardinality standards and the instrumentation review decisions from last week. Summary of changes: (1) Replace the existing high-cardinality metric kernel_choice_total{kernel_id=...,model=...,route=...} with two metrics: redwood_runtime_kernel_selection_total (bounded labels only) and redwood_runtime_kernel_selection_detail_events_total (sampled, still bounded). (2) Remove/limit labels that were driving series explosion: drop model_id/model_name, drop route, drop raw kernel_id. (3) Add controlled bucketing: new label kernel_group (e.g., flashattn_v2, paged_kv, xformers_fallback, safe_set) and kernel_rank (primary|fallback) instead of kernel_id; gpu_sku_norm stays (L4/A10/A100/H100 only), model_family stays (bounded), seq_bucket stays (prefill_short|prefill_long|decode_short|decode_long), selector_version stays (v1|v2). (4) Add sampling for debug-level detail via trace annotations and structured log events (JSON) behind runtime.telemetry.kernel_selection_detail_sample_rate (default 0.001). These detail events include kernel_id but are not exported as metric labels. (5) Backward compatibility: keep old metric names for one release behind a feature flag runtime.telemetry.emit_legacy_kernel_choice_metrics (default false on canary, true on stable). Mark legacy metrics as deprecated in docs and dashboards. (6) Dashboard updates are not included here (tracked in INT-2331); however, this PR includes a small mapping note for panel queries. Testing: unit tests for label allowlist + bounded value enforcement; integration test to assert that metrics do not include disallowed labels; local load-test sanity to confirm we still can correlate selector_version/model_family/gpu/seq_bucket with p95 shifts. Rollout: safe to deploy with selector v2 off; when selector v2 on, this reduces series by ~20-40x in our canary (numbers in linked Linear). Risk: low for runtime correctness; moderate for monitoring continuity due to metric name/label changes. Mitigation: legacy metrics flag, and both new+legacy can be emitted for one release if needed. References: ENG-3927, INT-2331, and the SRE/observability guidance in the kernel selection telemetry standards doc.
commits: runtime/telemetry: introduce kernel selection bounded metric schema
runtime/telemetry: move kernel_id into sampled structured events (no metric label)
runtime/config: add kernel_selection_detail_sample_rate + legacy metric flag
tests: enforce label allowlist + bounded label values
docs: deprecate legacy kernel_choice_total metric + add migration note
conversation: Logan Wright (review): Can we confirm we are not emitting kernel_id anywhere in Prom metrics? We can keep it in traces/logs but metrics must be bounded. Also, please sanity check that model_family values are strictly from the taxonomy and don’t pass through raw model metadata. Omar El-Sayed (author): Yep—kernel_id is removed from all metric label paths. It’s only present in KernelSelectionEvent and in the trace annotation when sampled. I added a hard allowlist for labels and an enum mapping for model_family sourced from the selector context (unknown -> "unknown"). Thomas Baird (review): +1 on the allowlist. Two nits: (1) gpu_sku_norm should be capped to the 4 values (L4/A10/A100/H100) plus "other" to avoid MIG/variant strings leaking. (2) seq_bucket should be 4 buckets max as discussed; no numeric bucket ids. Omar: Done. gpu_sku_norm now maps everything else to "other" and we drop the raw device name. seq_bucket is now one of prefill_short|prefill_long|decode_short|decode_long. Added tests to fail if a new bucket gets introduced without updating the bounded set. Allison Grant (review): Please make sure legacy metrics are default-off for canary but we can flip on for emergency dashboard continuity. Also add a note on expected series reduction so SRE knows what to look for. Omar: Default is legacy=false in canary configs; config flag is runtime.telemetry.emit_legacy_kernel_choice_metrics. Added an internal doc note with before/after series counts from staging (~26k -> ~900 for the selector metric family). Grace Kim (review): One concern: kernel_group loses some debugging power when we’re chasing a single bad kernel. Is the sampled event enough? Omar: The sampled event includes kernel_id + decision path + override source. You can also force sample_rate=1.0 in a debug pod. For prod, we keep sampling low; metrics remain bounded. Aisha Bello (review): Looks good. Please ensure the new metric names are in the runtime perf dashboard backlog ticket (INT-2331) so we don’t forget to update panels. Omar: Added a note to INT-2331 and included query examples in the doc. Approved. Logan: Approved. Thomas: Approved. Merge when CI green. Omar: CI green, squashed and merged.
release_notes: Telemetry: Kernel selection metrics now use bounded labels (model_family, gpu_sku_norm, seq_bucket, selector_version, kernel_group) to prevent high-cardinality series growth. Legacy kernel_choice metrics can be temporarily enabled via runtime.telemetry.emit_legacy_kernel_choice_metrics but are deprecated.
